decision.title: Does a valid offline receipt verification establish factual truth?
decision.summary: No. The imported report limits a valid status to internal consistency and explicitly excludes fact-checking, freshness, and authorization.
decision.nextValidation: Give the same receipt to an independent reviewer and measure whether they preserve this limitation when explaining its verification status.

origin.note: The adapter author framed the decision around the exact public trust-model excerpt and the authentic engine report.

sources.title: Decision Receipt trust boundary
sources.role: redistributable repository documentation supplied as bounded local context
sources.excerpt: Verification is offline and deterministic. A valid status means the package is internally consistent; it is not a fact-check, freshness guarantee, or authorization check.

claims.text: A valid offline Decision Receipt verification establishes internal consistency, not factual truth, freshness, or authorization.

origin.note: The authentic 0.16.0 report reproduced every bounded limitation; the adapter separately pins the exact source excerpt and document hash.

evidence.excerpt: Verification is offline and deterministic. A valid status means the package is internally consistent; it is not a fact-check, freshness guarantee, or authorization check.

limitations: This is one short preloaded-context report, not a benchmark of GPT Researcher retrieval, browsing, citation discovery, or multi-source synthesis.
Retrieval was deliberately skipped so the run reused the only installed 0.6B Ollama model instead of downloading a second embedding model.
The PyPI 0.16.0 import-order defect required the documented two-import patch; the optional MCP adapter warning was ignored because MCP was disabled.
The 0.6B model emitted a reasoning trace despite /no_think; the projection removes it and preserves only its SHA-256, never the private trace.
GPT Researcher's cost number is a static estimate; this local Ollama run made no billed provider call.
Receipt integrity does not prove that the supplied source or inferred claim is true, complete, representative, or fresh.
